Field Notes

A heron at the weir

The heron stood on one leg for almost an hour before it moved. Watching a patient bird teaches more about attention than any book on the subject, and the weir is quiet on weekday mornings.

Learning the oaks

There are two native oaks in these woods and they are easy to tell apart once you look at the stalks of the acorns and the shape of the leaf base. It takes one afternoon to learn, and a lifetime to stop noticing.
